title: The Secret of Secrets
author: Dan Brown
notes: Pretty good. The newest installment in the Robert Langdon series.

title: Digital Fortress
author: Dan Brown
notes: This one was a tough read. Too many glaring inconsistencies with reality.

title: Flash Boys
author: Michael Lewis
notes: Fun read. Provides interesting insights into the world of High Frequency Trading

title: Origin
author: Dan Brown
notes: Interesting read. The main thing I didn't like is that a cliff-hanger spans almost the whole book. I had to spoil it for myself after enough teasing of the big reveal.

title: Inferno
author: Dan Brown
notes: Pretty good one. Another Robert Langdon book.

title: The Da Vinci Code
author: Dan Brown
notes: Interesting read. Provocative from a religious standpoint.

title: Angels & Demons
author: Dan Brown
notes: The first Robert Langdon book, and in my opinion, the best one.

title: The Art of War
author: Sun Tzu
notes: I had been looking forward to this one but ultimately found it underwhelming. It it just a collection of insights about armed conflict.

title: Ghost Wars
author: Steve Coll
notes: Interesting content, but tough read. It details CIA activities in the Middle East that preceded and motivated the 9/11 attack.

title: The Source
author: James Michener
notes: A mammoth book, but an incredible story.

title: The Screwtape Letters
author: C.S. Lewis
notes: A creative idea: a senior demon writing letters to instruct his nephew on how to lead a human into temptation. It was recommended to me, but I found it just okay.

title: Outliers
author: Malcolm Gladwell
notes: Intriguing read. Sensible explanation for the why some individuals among us are outliers.

title: The Running Man
author: Stephen King
notes: Sort of a fun story, but not a favorite. Book was about the same caliber as the movie that was eventually made, 6.4/10 on IMDB.

title: Never Split the Difference
author: Chris Voss
notes: Interesting read by a former FBI hostage negotiator.

title: Holly
author: Stephen King
notes: I had high hopes for this one when I heard it was in development. Ultimately I was underwhelmed

title: The Long Walk
author: Stephen King
notes: Pretty entertaining read. The movie wasn't bad either, better than its 6.7/10 IMDB rating. Oddly, the movie significantly altered the ending, perhaps to make it more cinematic.

title: Salem's Lot
author: Stephen King
notes: I didn't care for it.

title: Dolores Claiborne
author: Stephen King
notes: Entertaining and a unique style. The story is told as a continuous, breathless, unedited, first-person monologue.

title: Hawaii
author: James Michener
notes: It took me an entire year to read this book. It is an incredible tale of Hawaii, from the origin of the islands to the mid-1900s. One of James Michener's best.

title: Finders Keepers
author: Stephen King
notes: An excellent read. Years later, I still vividly remember many details of the story.

title: Mr. Mercedes
author: Stephen King
notes: Fun. Intriguing. A good read. The first in a series featuring detective Bill Hodges.

title: The Innocent Man
author: Josh Grisham
notes: Non-fiction tale about a man freed from conviction by DNA evidence after 11 years on death row.

title: End of Watch
author: Stephen King
notes: Third book in the Bill Hodges trilogy. It was decent, but I didn't care much for the paranormal activity content when the first two books didn't have any.

title: Cujo
author: Stephen King
notes: I heard positive things about this one, but it just did not land for me.

title: The Outsider
author: Stephen King
notes: This one was pretty good. Quite a mystery and fairly entertaining throughout.

author: Stephen King
notes: One of the best books I've ever read. A man goes back in time to attempt to prevent the assassination of President John F. Kennedy on 11/22/63. It's a lengthy book, but it hooks you in right away and there is rarely a dull moment.
